title: Biological Classification
seo_title: Biological Classification Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_text: Five kingdom classification; salient features and classification of Monera, Protista and Fungi into major groups; lichens; viruses and viroids.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 2 Biological Classification: the five kingdoms, bacteria, protists, fungi, lichens, viruses, viroids and diseases they cause. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
key_sub: Viruses are not truly living outside a host cell.
body_html:
How to think about it

Whittaker's five kingdoms are based on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition and reproduction. Monera are prokaryotes (bacteria, cyanobacteria, archaebacteria, mycoplasma). Protista are unicellular eukaryotes such as diatoms, dinoflagellates, Euglena and protozoans.

Fungi are heterotrophs with chitin walls, grouped into phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes. Lichens are alga + fungus. Viruses are nucleoprotein particles that multiply only in host cells; viroids are bare RNA and prions are misfolded proteins.

Example

Penicillium: which class?

sac fungi

Answer: Ascomycetes

Example

Malaria is caused by?

a protozoan

Answer: Plasmodium

Common mistakes

  • Putting viruses in Monera.
  • Calling fungi plants.
  • Confusing viroids (RNA) with prions (protein).

faq.q: Why are viruses not placed in any kingdom?
faq.a: They are not cells and cannot reproduce or show metabolism outside a host cell.
